contracts.name: Host property and asset view v1
contracts.compatibility: Optional summary fields may be added; partition, cursor or redaction semantic changes require a new contract version.

interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.

failureSemantics: Fail closed when HOST authorization/profile resolution or effective party projection is unavailable.

Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

interfaces: Version every externally consumed operation or event and state its owner, caller, compatibility rule, timeout, and stable error behavior.
Keep fixtures deterministic and free of production credentials or customer data.
dataOwnership: This task owns only the named contract, UI, or infrastructure artifacts; authoritative domain rows remain in their service database.
stateMachine: Artifact lifecycle is DRAFT -> VALIDATED -> PUBLISHED; an incompatible semantic change requires a new version.
A failed validation remains unpublished and produces an actionable diagnostic.
Rollback selects the last validated artifact and does not mutate its contents.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM contract catalogue or the explicit ADMIN SITE/BRANCH partition used by the tested operation.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; DOCUMENT, PII, and INTERNAL_AUDIT appear only in explicitly granted test cases.

failureSemantics: Fail validation or startup when a required contract, environment value, or dependency is absent.
Never print tokens, presigned URLs, private document fields, or production values in test output.
Use stable assertion messages so a weak agent can locate the failing contract or scenario.
idempotencyConcurrency: Fixtures use unique deterministic business keys and cleanup is safe to repeat.
Repeated publication of identical canonical input produces the same fingerprint.
Concurrent API examples assert one effect or an explicit conflict.
